title: Basket proportionality test -- does the knockout move content-true ASR by what its installation effect implies?
why_this_exists: CONT-ENTRY 116 withdrew the button version (C-CONT-083) because the scope was never declared and was silently mixed inside one ratio: an all-slots numerator over a slot0 denominator. The result was +0.0221 (P=0.0022) on all slots and -0.0044 (P=0.59) on the declared slot0 primary. This document fixes every free choice BEFORE the basket numbers are computed, so that outcome cannot recur.
why_basket: Its measured arm is HARDWARE-MATCHED -- cbkasr base/ko/ctrl all ran on RTX A5000 at n-503, submitted together. The button arms span three GPUs (C-CONT-053). CONT-ENTRY 113 wrongly stated basket lacked a dose-0 ASR arm; tsb66bj_C_n0 is complete and judged (C-CONT-084).

SCOPE_DECLARED_UP_FRONT.slots: slot0 ONLY, applied IDENTICALLY to every one of the six quantities. This is the primary declared in CONT-ENTRY 094 for the dose ladder and it is inherited here without change.
SCOPE_DECLARED_UP_FRONT.reference_arm: ko - ctrl on BOTH sides. REVIEW-6/R6-01: the button test paired an installation numerator of ko-base with an ASR numerator of ko-ctrl3. Mixing reference arms inside one ratio is not permitted here.
SCOPE_DECLARED_UP_FRONT.scale: probability (C-CONT-073). The log-odds value is reported beside it, never instead of it.
SCOPE_DECLARED_UP_FRONT.all_slots_secondary: an all-slots version MAY be reported as a secondary and MUST be labelled as such

statistic: gap = measured(ko-ctrl ASR) - predicted, where predicted = -(ko-ctrl installation) * (ASR dose slope / installation dose slope). Joint domain bootstrap, 4000 resamples, the SAME domain indices used for all six quantities in each resample.

decision_rule.SUPPORTED: gap CI excludes zero on the slot0 PRIMARY
decision_rule.NOT SUPPORTED: gap CI includes zero on the primary, whatever the secondary shows

things_that_must_not_be_said: that a positive gap demonstrates installation does not drive attack success -- the dose contrast and the knockout act on different things (dose removes demonstrations, the knockout removes one row's ACCESS to them), and REVIEW-6 measured the within-dose-4 slope at -0.053, opposite in sign to the chord this test uses

that the test is unconfounded -- the basket ko arm's refusal rate must be reported beside the result, because on button ko refused 4.0% against ctrl3's 11.2% and conditioning on non-refusal collapsed the effect
that a two-point dose slope is a slope -- it is a chord across a curve A14 shows saturating
